svg.title: claudia composes — the object layer: where the code goes, and why
svg.desc: Layers from the core model through the server wire, the web client's session, pure helpers and components, the layout library, the desktop shell manifest and import/export, each with what is built, what this patch adds and what wrap would add; and the three ways of laying out lines around an object.
svg.text: claudia composes — the object layer: where the code goes, and why
Architecture for review. Green: already there. Iris: this patch. Rose, dashed: proposed for the wrap work, not built. File names are the repo's.
Core: the one object model

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: packages/claudia-core/src/claudia_core/objects.py
built
ObjectBody (kind, size, style, words, rotation) + a per-app anchor; BlockAnchor(block, offset, dx, dy) since D1023; the commands
AddObject, MoveObject, ResizeObject, RotateObject, DefineImage; the stacking order.
proposed
BlockAnchor gains wrap ('over' | 'around' | 'above-below' | 'behind', default 'over') and gap. Move already replaces the whole
anchor, so no new command; old documents read as 'over'.
Server: composes' wire

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: packages/claudia-server/src/claudia_server/composes.py, object_methods.py
built
add_image, add_rendering, move_object(block, offset, dx?, dy?), resize_object, rotate_object, remove_object; reads objects,
images, shapes; events objects, image, shape. IN_TEXT is the placement: a block id and a character.
proposed
set_wrap(id, wrap, gap) → MoveObject with the old anchor and the new wrap, so the history reads 'Wrap text around Picture 1'.
Import/export read and write it.
methods down, events up (JSON over the document's link)
Web client: session and the pure parts

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: web/app/lib/
this patch
text-session.ts: shapes (loaded, and kept by the 'shape' event); placeOf (the server counts characters, the page UTF-16 units);
addImage (creates' add_image with a place in the text).
this patch
text-containers.ts: floatBox (anchor character + dx/dy, kept in the column), columnOf, letsGoOfObject. text-object-look.ts:
lookOf, what any kind of object looks like as plain data. images.ts: PictureImport, pictureSize (the server allows one unit of
aspect error).
built
objects.ts shared types (BlockAnchor now has dx, dy); descriptions.ts (what a screen reader says); rendering.ts; neighbour,
resizedBy.
proposed
text-wrap.ts: which side of the column an object is on and the float box for the flow view (stage 2 below); pure and tested like
the rest.
Web client: components

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: web/app/components/
this patch
TextContainers.vue: draws every kind (lookOf) at floatBox; selection, keys, grip. TextEditor.vue: spotOf (the rect of the anchor
character via a Range), and a capture handler that lets go of the selection on any press or focus outside an object.
this patch
ImageImportDialog.vue: one dialog for all three apps; it takes an add(picture, aspect) function. SheetImageImportDialog.vue is
gone. TextWorkspace.vue: Edit ▸ Image… (Ctrl+Alt+I), addPicture.
proposed
A 'wrap band' hint on the held object in the editor and the Wrap Text… popover (Format menu). Dragging to set dx/dy (open point
1 of the layer mock-up).
built
RenderedFace / RenderedEditor (containers), the dock, the menus (document-menus.ts), keys.generated.ts.
Layout library: one deterministic engine

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: layout/src/
this patch
apps/composes.ts layoutText: an object's place is its character's spot plus px(dx), px(dy), kept inside the margins and above
the bottom margin. Before, dx/dy were ignored in print.
built
apps/objects.ts drawObject (box, picture, shape, words, rotation); flow/paginate.ts (paginate, locate); text/* (layoutParagraph:
a fixed width per paragraph).
proposed
flow/exclusions.ts: bands from object boxes plus the gap, in the order of the text. layoutParagraph takes widthAt(lineTop,
lineHeight) instead of one width; paginate hands it the bands that reach its page. Pure, integers in mpt, so the same
everywhere.
Desktop shells and the key table

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: clients/linux/src/claudia_shell_gtk/manifest.py, scripts/generate_keys.py
this patch
edit.image in composes' Edit menu (the same id and key in all three apps); keys.generated.ts and keyboard-shortcuts.md
regenerated; test_manifest's web-parity test caught the missing entry. The i18n catalogs (po/claudia.pot, de.po,
public/i18n/de.json) take the one new label.
proposed
format.wrap-text (Ctrl+Alt+L, free in the three manifests); Windows and macOS generate their menus from the manifest.
Import and export

text.font-family: JetBrains Mono, DejaVu Sans Mono, monospace

svg.text: Word (docx) and OpenDocument (odt)
built
Pictures and text boxes arrive by import as objects (D907). The importers were not read for this sheet, so what they keep of a
wrap, or of an offset, is not known yet.
proposed
wrap ↔ wrapNone / wrapSquare / wrapTopAndBottom + behindDoc ↔ style:wrap; what Claudia does not model (tight, through) is kept
and written back.
The decision: who lays out the lines round an object
Wrap changes where lines break, and lines are laid out twice today: by the browser in the
editor and by the engine in print and the print preview. Everything else in this layer is
the same for all three options.
Wrap in print only
least work; the editor lies
editor: browser
print: engine
The engine wraps (exclusions in layoutParagraph); the
editor keeps showing objects over the words.
A held object shows a dashed band where the words will
make room.
Cost: small. Risk: what you see is not what prints, for
exactly the objects that matter.
The engine lays out the editor too
exact; a rewrite
editor: engine
print: engine
The page view draws the engine's display list; a caret,
a selection, input methods, spell checking and the
screen-reader tree are rebuilt on top of it.
Cost: months, and the risk is in accessibility (BITV)
and in typing with an input method.
Gain: one set of lines, everywhere, as the vision
statement asks.
Engine exact, floats in the editor — in two stages
recommended
editor: floats
print + preview: engine
Stage 1 as option 1 (print and the print preview are
exact).
Stage 2: a non-editable float of the object's size sits
at the anchor's line in the editor (the editor already
has such nodes: peer carets, replies). CSS floats wrap
on one side only, so an object in the middle of the
column wraps on its wider side in the flow view; print
and the preview show both sides.
A test feeds the same text and objects to both and
compares which lines are narrowed.
Why option 3
· The owner's rule is that a document renders identically wherever the engine renders it; the
browser's editor has never been that, and does not have to be as long as it is honest about
it.
· It keeps contenteditable, which is where typing, input methods, spell checking and the
screen-reader reading order come from.
· Wrap that is only in print (stage 1) is already worth having for Word and LibreOffice files
that arrive with wrapped pictures.
· Open: whether stage 2 is wanted before people complain. Recommended: wait for the complaint,
and build stage 1 first.
